faq.a: The distance from Puerto Banús to Sotogrande is roughly 20 nautical miles (about 37 km). At a cruising speed of 20–25 knots, the journey takes around 50–60 minutes each way. This makes a full-day charter ideal for the polo final, giving you time to cruise, anchor for lunch, and still arrive in time for the match.

data.body_html:
Planning to attend the Sotogrande Polo Final 2045? Make it an unforgettable day by arriving in style on a private boat. A Marbella boat rental from Puerto Banús to Sotogrande is not just transport—it's the highlight of your trip. Cruise past the Golden Mile, anchor for a swim, and arrive at the polo fields relaxed and ready. Here's everything you need to know.

Why take a boat to the Sotogrande Polo Final?

The Sotogrande Polo Final is one of the most anticipated events on the Costa del Sol social calendar. With traffic on the AP-7 often gridlocked, a boat is the smartest way to travel. The journey from Puerto Banús to Sotogrande is around 20 nautical miles—roughly 37 km—and takes under an hour at cruising speed. You'll skip the stress and arrive with a tan.

Our fleet for the polo final

We have a range of boats departing from Puerto Banús, all with licensed skippers and full inclusions. Here are the best options for groups heading to the polo:

  • Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) – ideal for smaller groups, €749/2h or €2,299/8h
  • Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) – same price as Astondoa, slightly more space
  • Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) – the showstopper, includes a free jet ski, €4,719 for 4h minimum
  • Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) – great for entertaining
  • Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) – ultimate luxury for a big group

All other boats (Bandido, Canados 86, Dubhe, Fairline Targa, K80, Lagoon 380, Mariah SX21, Pershing 46, Red Tide, Speedboat, Maiora 26m) are available on request—just message us on WhatsApp for pricing.

What's included on every charter

No hidden costs. Every booking includes:

  • Licensed skipper and fuel
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava
  • Light snacks
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%)

For the Mangusta 80, a jet ski is also included free—perfect for a pre-polo adrenaline rush.

The route: from Puerto Banús to Sotogrande

Depart from Puerto Banús and head south-west along the coast. Pass the golden sands of Cabopino, the cliffs of Cala del Faro, and the exclusive marina of Estepona. About 50–60 minutes later, you'll see the Sotogrande marina ahead. Your skipper will anchor off the Guadiaro river mouth—the best spot to enjoy the sea breeze before heading ashore.

How to plan your day

For a typical afternoon final (4–6 PM), leave Puerto Banús at 11:00 AM. Cruise for an hour, stop for a swim at Cala Cortés, enjoy lunch on board, and arrive at Sotogrande by 2:30 PM. From the marina, it's a short taxi ride to the polo club. After the match, return to your boat for a sunset cruise back—unforgettable.

Why book early?

The polo final attracts thousands of visitors, and boats get booked weeks in advance. Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39) are fixed at €749/2h or €2,299/8h—no surprises. For the Mangusta 80, the minimum charter is 4 hours at €4,719, which includes the jet ski. Don't leave it to the last minute; secure your boat now.

Other events to pair with your charter

If you're in Marbella for the polo, why not extend your boating adventure? Combine your trip with a visit to the [Marbella boat rental hub](/blog/) or explore our [Puerto Banús charter options](/boat-rental-puerto-banus/). You could also plan a day trip to [Estepona](/) or [Cabopino](/). And for the ultimate luxury, check out our Mangusta 80 guide.

Book your Marbella boat rental for Sotogrande Polo Final 2045

Ready to make this polo season unforgettable? Contact us on WhatsApp with your preferred date and group size. We'll confirm availability and send you the exact price. For Tier A boats, it's a flat €749/2h or €2,299/8h. For the Mangusta 80, it's €4,719 for 4 hours. All charters depart from Puerto Banús. See you on the water!
